items.title: [outstatic] Outstatic: Authenticated GitHub REST proxy can send OAuth token to non-GitHub origins
items.summary: ImpactOutstatic’s authenticated GitHub REST proxy accepted an unvalidated endpoint parameter and constructed an upstream GitHub API URL by string concatenation while attaching the authenticated user’s GitHub OAuth token.A user with access to the Outstatic dashboard could craft a request that caused the server to send their own GitHub OAuth token to a non-GitHub host. If that token was captured, it could be used to access GitHub resources available to that same user, including private repositories depending on granted scopes.This does not allow unauthenticated attackers to access private repository data, and it does not directly expose another user’s GitHub token without an additional same-origin execution or request-forging primitive.PatchesThe issue has been patched by validating that proxied requests resolve to the exact https://api.github.com/ origin and by restricting forwarded request headers.Users should upgrade to v2.2.1 or later.WorkaroundsIf upgrading immediately is not possible, restrict access to /api/outstatic/github to trusted dashboard users only, or temporarily disable the endpoint if it is not needed.As a temporary code-level mitigation, reject body-provided endpoint values that do not begin with /, verify the parsed URL origin is exactly https://api.github.com/, and block forwarding of sensitive headers such as Authorization, Host, and User-Agent.Users who suspect their token was exposed should revoke the affected GitHub OAuth authorization and sign in again.Referenceshttps://github.com/avitorio/outstatic/security/advisories/GHSA-7jvc-9xq8-frffhttps://github.com/avitorio/outstatic/commit/03b9147a04336986174ef0be1c300b3abbbec3e1https://github.com/avitorio/outstatic/releases/tag/v2.2.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7jvc-9xq8-frff

items.title: [@augment-vir/node] augment-virShell allows Command Injection in `grep()` via Unsanitized `searchPattern`
items.summary: Shell Command Injection in grep() via Unsanitized searchPatternSummaryThe grep() function exported by @augment-vir/node inserts caller-controlled search patterns directly into a double-quoted shell command string without sanitization (grep.ts:310). When the constructed command is passed to spawn() with shell: 'bash' (shell.ts:98-99), bash evaluates $() command substitution expressions embedded in the pattern, resulting in arbitrary OS command execution as the Node.js process user. Any downstream application that passes untrusted input to grep()'s pattern or patterns field is vulnerable to unauthenticated local (and potentially remote) code execution. CVSS Base Score: 7.8 (High).DetailsRoot cause: packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:310 maps each search pattern into the shell fragment -e "${searchPattern}" with no sanitization:// grep.ts:310...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e "${searchPattern}"`),The resulting full command string is forwarded to runShellCommand (grep.ts:320), which calls streamShellCommand (shell.ts:221-224), which ultimately calls:// shell.ts:98-99const childProcess = spawn(command, {    shell,   // defaults to 'bash' (shell.ts:92)Because shell is 'bash', bash interprets $() within the double-quoted pattern as a command substitution and executes it before grep ever runs.Incomplete sanitization: An escape() helper exists at grep.ts:178-180 but only replaces " with \" and removes newlines. It is applied to excludePatterns, excludeDirs, and includeFiles (grep.ts:297-308) but not to searchPatterns. Even if it were applied, double-quote escaping does not prevent $() or backtick substitution inside bash double-quote contexts.Data flow (source → sink):StepLocationDescription1packages/node/src/index.ts:3export * from './augments/fs/grep.js' — exposes grep() as a public npm API2packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:223-226grep() accepts caller-controlled grepSearchPattern and grepSearchLocation3packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:228searchPatterns derived from grepSearchPattern.patterns || [grepSearchPattern.pattern]4packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:269-314fullCommand built as a plain shell string5packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:310Sink: searchPattern inserted as `-e "${searchPattern}"` — no escaping applied6packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:320fullCommand passed to runShellCommand7packages/node/src/augments/terminal/shell.ts:221-224Forwarded to streamShellCommand8packages/node/src/augments/terminal/shell.ts:98-99spawn(command, { shell: 'bash' }) executes the constructed command stringSuggested remediation:--- a/packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts+++ b/packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts@@-function escape(input: string) {-    return input.replaceAll('"', String.raw`\"`).replaceAll('\n', '');+function shellQuote(input: string) {+    return `'${input.replaceAll("'", String.raw`'\''`).replaceAll('\n', '')}'`; }@@-        ...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e "${searchPattern}"`),+        ...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e ${shellQuote(searchPattern)}`),+        '--',         ...searchParts,Alternatively, replace the shell-string approach with spawn('grep', args, { shell: false }) to avoid shell interpretation entirely.PoCPrerequisites: Docker installed on the host. All steps run locally inside a container — no network exposure, no real credentials, no DoS.Step 1 — Build the Docker image:docker build -t augment-vir-vuln-001-poc \  vuln-001Step 2 — Run the exploit container:docker run --rm --name augment-vir-vuln-001-run augment-vir-vuln-001-pocCore exploit (exploit.mjs inside the container):import { grep } from '@augment-vir/node';await grep(  { pattern: '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match' },  { file: 'package.json' },);The $() shell substitution in the pattern causes bash to execute touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered before grep runs. The sentinel file is created even though the grep pattern itself matches nothing in package.json.Expected output:[*] Calling grep() with injected $() command substitution pattern...[*] Pattern: $(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match=== VULNERABLE ===[+] COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED: sentinel file exists at /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered[+] The $() substitution in pattern was executed by bash via spawn({shell:"bash"})Minimal reproduction without Docker:mkdir /tmp/av-grep-poc && cd /tmp/av-grep-pocnpm init -ynpm install @augment-vir/node@31.73.2cat > poc.mjs <<'EOF'import { grep } from '@augment-vir/node';await grep(  { pattern: '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-grep-poc)no-match' },  { file: 'package.json' },);EOFrm -f /tmp/augment-vir-grep-pocnode poc.mjstest -f /tmp/augment-vir-grep-poc && echo VULNERABLEVerification: Both Phase 1 static analysis and Phase 2 dynamic reproduction confirmed the vulnerability. VULNERABLE and COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED were observed in stdout; the sentinel file /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered was created inside the Docker container.ImpactThis is an OS Command Injection (CWE-78)
